summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Research design for a structured review of the small-state hedging literature (definitions, measurement, economic outcomes) and an option set for Nepal. The session web-search budget was exhausted and doi.org/Crossref are blocked, so no document was located or verified in r1; candidate references are listed in specific.literature_review as unverified bibliographic leads (authors, year, title, venue from general knowledge, flagged for verification) and are not cited as evidence. The option set is a labelled set of analytical alternatives for scenario design, not recommendations and not an assessment of any government's intentions.

findings.claim: What peer-reviewed studies find on economic outcomes (trade, FDI, aid, borrowing terms, growth volatility) associated with hedging versus alignment by small states.
findings.note: Requires located and verified peer-reviewed articles with stated samples, periods and identification strategies; none retrieved in r1.

findings.claim: Documented cases of economic coercion affecting small states (trade restrictions, border/transit disruptions, sanctions) and measured economic effects, incl. Nepal's 2015-16 border disruption.
findings.note: Requires peer-reviewed or official quantification; Nepal episode via NRB/customs monthly data (owned with 17A/21B).

findings.claim: Nepal-specific literature on foreign-policy balancing between India and China and on its economic effects.
findings.note: Locate peer-reviewed Nepal studies in r2; policy commentary is tier 7 and must be separated from empirical work.

findings.claim: Hedging is defined for this review as a set of mixed signals combining engagement and insurance toward competing powers while avoiding exclusive alignment; alternative definitions in the literature will be recorded and compared, not merged.
Economic outcomes are only attributed to hedging where a study presents an identification strategy; correlational or case-narrative evidence is labelled as such.
The option set is an analytical list for stress-testing (inputs to Agent 28 and scenario design), not advice to or a ranking of any government, party or leader.

data_gaps: Session WebSearch budget was exhausted before searches for this subagent could be run; Crossref/doi.org are blocked by the egress proxy. Leads marked 'catalog endpoint' are the unverified catalog URLs in research/sources/source_catalog.yaml, not search-located documents.
No peer-reviewed article on small-state hedging was located or verified in r1.
No quantitative dataset on economic coercion episodes (e.g. sanctions/coercion databases) located.
No Nepal-specific empirical study of foreign-policy balancing and economic outcomes located.

assumptions.text: Hedging definition follows the engagement-plus-insurance family of definitions; alternatives recorded separately.
Only studies with explicit identification strategies support causal claims.
Option set is analytical, not prescriptive, and makes no claim about private intentions of any government.

challenges.text: Enable Crossref/doi.org access or a bibliographic database for r2; academic source leads cannot be verified in the restricted network and the catalog 'academic' entry has no URL.
Request red-team review of the option set for omitted options and for implicit normative bias toward any partner.
No external variable in the 41-variable list captures coercion/disruption risk as a policy state; consider a dated-event variable feeding S02/S05 transit shocks.

uncertainty: Very high. No literature was retrieved or verified; the candidate reference list may contain bibliographic errors and is not evidence. The literature is expected to be largely qualitative with limited causal evidence on economic outcomes.

literature_review.method: Structured review: (1) define hedging and alternatives; (2) extract for each study: sample, period, outcome variables, method, finding direction (no numbers until retrieved); (3) separate empirical from conceptual work; (4) Nepal-specific subsection.

option_set.note: Options are stress-test alternatives for scenarios; not recommendations; no probabilities assigned.

options.label: Diversified engagement (status-quo balancing)
options.description: Parallel economic engagement with India, China, US, EU, Japan and others without exclusive commitments

options.label: Multilateral anchoring
options.description: Prioritise MDB/UN-system financing and rules-based trade frameworks to reduce bilateral exposure

options.label: Connectivity redundancy
options.description: Invest in alternative transit/trade/energy routes to reduce single-point-of-failure exposure (links to 16B SPOF list)

options.label: Closer economic alignment with one neighbour
options.description: Deeper integration with a single major neighbour; analysed as a stress-test alternative only

options.label: Labour-market diversification
options.description: Broaden G2G labour agreements (Korea EPS, Japan SSW, Europe) to reduce GCC/Malaysia concentration

option_set.trade_off_note: Each option to be assessed against all 12 welfare objectives (src/economic_model/welfare.py), not GDP alone, once evidence is retrieved.
